response.markdown_report:
Select **uniform multi-negative masked-target ranking** as the next experiment. At 10% progress, it offers a small, diagnosis-driven change while preserving corrected BERT4Rec.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) The supplied baseline scored 0.5425; terminal-allocation variants scored 0.4725 and 0.4925. These comparisons do not isolate masking effects, but provide no evidence for increasing terminal exposure. (2) Industrial and Electronics have negative tenth-percentile training margins, −0.2267 and −0.0479. This motivates investigating discrimination without claiming held-out improvement. (3) Users distinguish specific fit from broad relevance and find some movie recommendations insufficiently connected to their histories. Ranking objectives can test contextual discrimination, although interaction labels do not directly encode these judgments.

**Insights from related work.** (1) gSASRec identifies limitations of sampled BCE [2]. This motivates an objective experiment within BERT4Rec, without transferring its backbone. (2) R2NS cautions against immediate hardest-negative mining [3]. Uniform negatives offer a simpler first comparison. (3) AlterRec identifies optimization problems in ID/text fusion [4]. Scratch-trained text remains promising, but requires more implementation and validation than an objective change.

The framework separates three intervention axes:

| Direction | Intervention | Main uncertainty |
|---|---|---|
| Ranking supervision | Multi-negative cross-entropy | Sampled competitors may be false negatives |
| Item representation | Joint scratch-trained title residual | Sparse text and fusion imbalance |
| Temporal relevance | Learned historical time-gap biases | Recency benefit is unestablished |

Scores below are **originality / potential / user alignment / model alignment / difficulty**, each out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Uniform multi-negative ranking | 3/7/6/8/3 | Directly tests weak target separation with little architectural work | Cannot establish compatibility or current demand |
| Joint title residual | 4/7/8/6/6 | Could distinguish specific qualities and identifiable movie connections | Text coverage and optimization may limit benefit |
| Historical time-gap attention | 4/7/6/5/7 | Can learn relevance across irregular gaps | Supplied sensitivity results establish no temporal direction |

**Chosen experiment.** Keep masking, windows, architecture and optimizer fixed; replace the baseline objective with cross-entropy over each hidden positive and 16 uniformly sampled eligible negatives. This jointly changes objective and negative count, so any gain belongs to that combined intervention. It targets two user failures—broad adjacent matches displacing specific matches, and weakly supported movie choices—and the measured lower-tail ranking errors. These are hypotheses: sampled negatives need not resemble those user-described errors.

```
for each category, epoch, batch:
    sequence, targets = unchanged_corrected_sampler()
    negatives = uniform_eligible_items(targets, K=16)
    logits = score(hidden_target_features, [targets, negatives])
    loss = baseline_reduction(cross_entropy(logits, positive_index=0))
    update_one_BERT4Rec(loss)
```

Preserve seeds, all four routes, at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches/epoch. Retain one checkpoint/category, appended-mask inference, diagnostic APIs and predictor consistency. Select only by pinned macro validation HR@10; training margins are explanatory diagnostics.

References: [1] BERT4Rec; [2] gSASRec; [3] R2NS; [4] AlterRec. Links and qualifications accompany this report.

idea.description: Test uniform multi-negative masked-target cross-entropy in the supplied corrected BERT4Rec. Train exactly one independent model per category. Preserve baseline terminal-mask allocation and reconstruction corruption, replacing only the ranking objective and its negative count with a declared 16-negative candidate cross-entropy intervention.
idea.motivation: Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics have training-exposed negative-beats-positive rates of 12.03% and 10.25%, with negative tenth-percentile margins. More competing items per hidden target may improve contextual discrimination. The proposal explicitly targets two user-facing failures: broadly related adjacent products displacing specifically supported matches, and movie recommendations with weak identifiable connections to history. These links are hypotheses, not measured remedies: uniform negatives may be easy, and interaction supervision cannot establish ownership, compatibility, redundancy, or current intent. Earlier terminal-allocation proposals underperformed the supplied baseline, motivating an orthogonal objective experiment rather than another masking increase.
idea.implementation_notes:
Apply this intervention to the supplied baseline; its source is not included here, so this is an implementation specification rather than an executable train.py replacement. Preserve the BERT4Rec architecture, original sampled windows, eligible-user distribution, reserved-mask corruption, terminal allocation, optimizer, schedule, clipping and checkpoint-selection policy. Document the actual baseline loss reduction and preserve its weighting over valid positions and examples when reducing the new per-target cross-entropy.

For each valid masked target y, sample K=16 negatives independently with replacement from a uniform eligible training catalog. Exclude y and preserve the baseline's existing observed-history exclusions; do not silently introduce additional exclusions. Document the eligible-set definition and proposal q. Repeated negative draws are permitted and retain their multiplicity; record collision and unique-count statistics. Define the objective explicitly as cross-entropy over the positive and sampled negatives, with no logQ adjustment. This is a sampled candidate-ranking surrogate, not an unbiased full-catalog likelihood estimator or an application of Correcting the LogQ Correction. Unobserved items remain uncertain negatives. If an eligible set is empty, use the baseline's documented fallback and count occurrences. Keep reserved PAD and MASK outside the negative catalog.

The treatment changes both negative count and objective; do not attribute improvements to either component separately. A later, separately budgeted comparison can match negative counts between objectives. Do not add hard mining, temporal biases, text features, new masking allocation or auxiliary fitted scores to this primary experiment.

Use preprocessing seed 0 and training seed 42; retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, single-GPU execution, at most 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. Respect the host's SASREC_EPOCHS=200 default. All training, diagnostics and failures count against 43,200 GPU-seconds. Never read other trials or reuse their checkpoints.

Prediction loads exactly one selected model/checkpoint per category. Retain the final L-1 history events, append MASK, left-pad, and read the greatest nonpadding position, never count-1. Hide all supervised target occurrences at their selected positions during bidirectional training; legitimate earlier repetitions remain historical context. Preserve the predictor writer, architecture configuration, mappings and routing. Fresh-process checkpoint/predictor score parity must be measured before claiming it.

Preserve family-specific sample_batch and ModelView, including view.model as the actual trained module, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Diagnostic loader tuples remain (None, sequence, positive, negative), with B x L tensors; training-only multi-negative tensors can remain internal to the loss. Preserve the original one-negative diagnostic protocol for comparability, distinguishing it from the training negative pool. Report measured margin tails and error rates, without treating them as held-out gains. Missing sampler provenance, fresh-process parity and attention deletion remain unavailable until implemented and measured.

Select using only the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 and the unchanged host-compatible selection schedule. Do not fabricate a new validation score. Available data comprise public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps; unavailable ratings, review text, item categories/prices/stores and simulator traits must not enter training or diagnostics.
idea.pseudocode:
Preserve supplied preprocessing(seed=0), splits and dataset routing.
Declare K=16, unchanged masking policy and unchanged checkpoint-selection rule.
For each of the four categories:
    Initialize one supplied corrected BERT4Rec with training seed 42.
    For epoch in range(at_most_200):
        For step in range(200):
            Sample original windows using the unchanged baseline sampler.
            Construct unchanged corrected masked inputs and valid target labels.
            features = model.log2feats(sequence)[valid_target_positions]
            For each positive target y:
                eligible = baseline_uniform_eligible_catalog_excluding(y)
                negatives = sample_with_replacement(eligible, 16)
                logits = model.predict_score(features_y, [y] + negatives)
                target_loss = cross_entropy(logits, class_index=0)
            loss = baseline_target_and_example_reduction(target_losses)
            Apply unchanged optimizer, schedule and clipping.
        Apply unchanged host-compatible checkpoint-selection procedure.
    Save exactly one selected checkpoint and its matching configuration.
Emit the matching working/predict.py with all four category routes.
For inference:
    sequence = left_pad(last_L_minus_1(history) + [MASK], L)
    position = greatest_index_where(sequence != PAD)
    features = model.log2feats(sequence)[position]
    return model.predict_score(features, candidate_items)
Retain existing diagnostic APIs and their one-negative comparison protocol.
Obtain macro validation HR@10 only from the pinned host evaluator.
Never combine independently trained predictions or average checkpoints.

originality.positive: A narrowly controlled objective experiment connects the observed lower-tail errors to a practical BERT4Rec intervention while avoiding further masking changes.
originality.negative: Multi-negative cross-entropy is established; its use here is an experimental adaptation rather than a new algorithm.

future_potential.positive: A useful result could motivate count-matched objective controls and subsequent controlled negative-sampling research within the same backbone.
future_potential.negative: Uniform negatives may offer limited discrimination, and gains on sampled validation may not transfer to full-catalog user usefulness.

code_difficulty.positive: The change is confined mainly to negative sampling and the training loss, preserving architecture and inference.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct eligible-set handling, loss weighting, diagnostic comparability and runtime accounting still require careful integration with the unavailable host source.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Establishes bidirectional masked-item reconstruction and prediction using a terminal mask.
Provides the backbone and leakage-prevention principles retained in the proposal.
limitations: Terminal supervision is already part of BERT4Rec; increasing its allocation is not a new backbone.
Does not establish the proposed objective's benefit under the supplied RecHarness protocol.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: The supplied search summary identifies sampled-BCE overconfidence and training instability as reasons to investigate the objective.
limitations: Its findings do not establish that candidate cross-entropy improves corrected BERT4Rec.
Its backbone must not replace the required BERT4Rec family.

related_work.title: R2NS
contributions: The supplied summary motivates uniform warm-up and controlled negative difficulty rather than immediate hardest-negative selection.
limitations: Its curriculum and retrieval machinery are deferred to keep the first experiment small.

related_work.title: AlterRec
contributions: The supplied summary identifies ID dominance and undertrained text representations as risks in naive ID/text fusion.
limitations: Its separate optimization approach is not directly transferred to the required jointly trained single-model setting.
Does not demonstrate gains for a scratch-trained text extension under this benchmark.
